# LocalXiv 0.0.19
Read arXiv papers comfortably on your Mac, then take them to Kindle. This preview converts more papers from their TeX source, draws TikZ and commutative diagrams, and no longer gives up on a whole paper for one small defect.
## Changes
- **More papers convert.** In the 100-paper test corpus, 61 papers now convert from their TeX source, up from 47. Papers that need arXiv's rendered HTML go from 18 to 22, and papers that end with only the original PDF go from 34 to 17. - **Diagrams.** TikZ pictures, `tikzcd` and `xymatrix` diagrams, and inline `\tikz` drawings now show as images. Before, the reader lost them, and a diagram inside an equation stopped the conversion. - **Math and tables.** A `$` in a TeX comment or an escaped `\$` no longer breaks the math after it, which turned some tables into plain text. An equation after a colon in a heading or caption stays in the heading. - **One defect no longer fails the paper.** Up to 3 equations that no renderer can draw stay as their TeX, and the conversion report lists them. A link to a heading that the conversion lost becomes plain text. A repeated bibliography key, a translated second abstract, and a few commands that arXiv could not expand are accepted with a warning. - **Figures.** Old PostScript (`.ps`) figures now convert to images. - **arXiv HTML.** More of arXiv's own renders are accepted: figures and links inside SVG drawings, figure captions beside their image, and text inside math. - **Cleanup.** Unused code that an architecture review found is removed.
## Verification and limitations
The release workflow checks the source, builds the portable app, runs native renderer tests, and verifies the packaged runtime after moving the app. Attached assets include the verification report, runtime inventory, exact app source, dependency source inputs, and SHA-256 checksums.
For this release, the 100-paper parser corpus ran on the release code against 0.0.18. The component tests did not run. Every finding that the corpus reports as new was traced: each one is a later defect that a fix exposed, or a known false positive of the corpus checks.
Open items:
- 17 papers in the corpus still end with only the original PDF. The audit in `docs/parser-audit-2026-10-15.md` lists their causes. - The local LaTeXML fallback is version 0.8.8, which cannot read the TeX Live 2026 packages that many papers load. It converted no corpus paper in this release. - A paper that keeps an equation as TeX shows that TeX as text. A paper whose heading was lost shows the link as plain text. - The corpus uses Pandoc 3.12.1 and EPUBCheck 5.4.0. The app bundles Pandoc 3.11 and EPUBCheck 5.3.0, so a paper that converts in the corpus can still fail in the app. - Code listings with a `style=` option can fail EPUB validation.
Offline tests use scripted provider responses. They verify recovery and export behavior, not live-provider reliability, scientific accuracy, generation speed, or cost.
AI explanations remain experimental. Generation may take several minutes or fail, and generated claims need checking against the paper. AI requests send selected paper content to your configured provider and may incur charges. Paper search sends the typed text to Semantic Scholar and arXiv. Importing, reading, and exporting papers do not require AI credentials.
## Installation
Requires Apple Silicon and macOS 26 or newer. Download the DMG and drag LocalXiv into Applications. Finish active jobs before updating. Your library and settings remain on your Mac. Updater-enabled builds can use **LocalXiv → Check for Updates…** once the signed feed is published.
This preview is ad hoc signed, without Apple Developer ID signing or notarization. macOS may block the first launch. The Sparkle update feed is signed separately with the project's local update key. Separate-Mac installation and actual Kindle delivery are not covered by the automated checks.
